labeled_steps.reasoning_step:
Let the four positive constants be a1 = 18, a2 = 72, a3 = 98, a4 = k, and write
N(x) = (x − a1)(x − a2)(x − a3)(x − a4),
so f(x) = N(x)/x for x > 0.
labeled_steps.label: Understanding the Problem

labeled_steps.reasoning_step:
Critical points of f on (0, ∞) occur where
f'(x) = 0 ⇔ (N'(x) x − N(x))/x^2 = 0
⇔ N'(x) x = N(x).
labeled_steps.label: Execute Solving Strategy and Calculate

labeled_steps.reasoning_step:
Since N'(x) = Σ Π_{j≠i} (x − a_j) and multiplying by x and rearranging gives the equivalent rational equation
Σ a_i/(x − a_i) = 0.
Multiplying through by the product Π (x − a_i) yields the cubic polynomial
P(x) = Σ a_i Π_{j≠i} (x − a_j),
whose three real roots x1 < x2 < x3 are exactly the three critical points of f on (0, ∞). (Because all a_i are positive and distinct, there is exactly one root of Σ a_i/(x − a_i) in each interval between adjacent a_i.)
